author: BBC News
description:
Iran and the US appear to be returning to all-out war, after 10 nights of escalating US airstrikes, and growing Iranian reprisals. 

The Pentagon has confirmed that almost 100 US service personnel have been injured in the conflict in the past fortnight, while three US soldiers have been killed. 

Iran’s revolutionary guards have targeted US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain and carried out more attacks on tankers in the strait of Hormuz.  Commercial shipping through the key shipping lane has again come to a standstill, putting further pressure on global energy supplies. 

Yemen’s Houthis, who are backed by Iran, have announced a maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, further threatening transit of oil and natural gas. 

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Jeremy Bowen and Sarah Smith.

author: BBC News
description:
US President Donald Trump has imposed a 50% tariff on a wide range of goods imported from Canada, in retaliation for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.
 
Everyday consumer items like wine and hockey sticks and industrial goods such as cement are among the goods targeted. However, several key exports will be spared, such as energy, potash, critical minerals and fish.
 
Prime Minister Mark Carney responded by saying Canada stood ready to "intensify" trade talks with the US in the coming weeks.

author: BBC News
description:
Warning: Mention of suicide. 

Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party.
 
It is demanding an overhaul of India's education system after a medical entrance exam, taken by 2.28 million students, was cancelled following reports that the paper had leaked. A re-test was held weeks later.
 
More than 20 students have since died by suicide, with their families saying they were devastated by the scandal.
 
The movement has made the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan a key demand.
 
Protests saw overwhelming violence, with protesters wounded when police used batons and tear gas on them.

Last week, Poland scrambled fighter jets after Russian aircraft was spotted over the Baltic Sea. We ask Vitaly Shevchenko, chief analyst for BBC Monitoring, why the Kremlin is flexing its muscles so close to Nato countries, and how Europe views the threat of Russian aggression, more than four years after Vladimir Putin launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

author: BBC News
description:
The US military says it launched another round of strikes against Iran to "further degrade" its capabilities to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The strikes - the 10th consecutive night of attacks - come after US President Donald Trump vowed to punish Iran for the deaths of US soldiers.

In response, Iran said it struck two oil tankers in the waterway, as well as US military assets in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, state news agency IRNA reported.
President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was now fighting a "full-scale war" with the US. Trump earlier said Iran had been hit "very hard" the previous night "in honour" of three US soldiers killed recently - two in Jordan and one in Iraq.

US Central Command (Centcom) said its latest strikes had hit Iranian "military command centres, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defence systems".

Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Cockroach Janta Party, a youth-led movement seeking education reforms and resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
 
Tens of thousands of young men and women had turned up for Monday's protest and tried to march on parliament, defying a police ban.
 
Central Delhi witnessed overwhelming violence, with at least 60 protesters wounded when police used batons and tear gas on them. Policemen also tore down the stage and makeshift tents at the main protest venue.
 
Police said 118 of their personnel were also injured and 70 protesters have been detained.
